newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude trades sideways in slow day.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude trades sideways in slow day.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were treading water in a thin market on Thursday as public holidays across Europe drained liquidity and the U.S give little direction.
June IPE Brent was trading 2 cents lower at $18.50 a barrel at 1510 GMT while May IPE gas oil was 75 cents off at $171.00 a tonne.
"It (Brent) is really doing nothing, we have the holidays in Europe quietening everything down," said one trader.
One analyst said the market was poised on a cusp.
"We are waiting to break over the next two to three days and it could go either way," he said.
Brent had good support at $18.30 a barrel and then $18.20 with resistance at $18.77, traders said. Selling pressure was likely to surface once the contract started to approach $18.75.
WTI was trading at $20.21 a barrel, down one cent after mild profit taking after the June contract managed a high of $20.29.
"WTI is holding the trendline at the bottom," said one dealer.
Resistance is seen initially at $20.39 and then $20.50.
